Name: Oncolys BioPharma Inc.
Description:
Oncolys BioPharma Inc. is a Tokyo-based bioventure established in Japan in March 2004. Its mission is to contribute to the advancement of medical science in the world through bringing innovation to the existing treatments for cancer and serious infectious diseases, using its virology-based new drug discovery technologies.

The company operates in two business segments. Pharmaceutical Business segment is engaged in the research, development, manufacture and marketing of novel drugs. Its major pipeline Telomelysin (OBP-301), an oncolytic adenovirus immunotherapy is in clinical development targeting various types of solid tumors including melanoma , HCC and esophageal cancer. Along with Telomelysin, an anti-HIV drug OBP-601 (Censavudine) and a novel HDAC inhibitor OBP-801 are also under development in the United States. Diagnostics Business segment is engaged in the research, development, manufacture and marketing of CTC (Circulating Tumor Cell) detection adenovirus TelomeScan, as well as the provision of inspection services. 

 Oncolys was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Mothers Market in December 2014 and has a clinical laboratory center in Kobe, Japan and a subsidiary in New Jersey, USA.
Location: Fort Lee, New Jersey, United States

Name: DNALabs
Description: We are committed to providing genetic testing solutions to help everyone know more about themselves. Our DNA holds critical and unique information about us, including how we interact with our environment including medicine, and allows us to optimize treatment outcomes that are best suited for each of us.

Name: Analiza
Description: Founded in 1996 in Cleveland, OH, Analiza, Inc. is a leading US based provider of high quality, affordable analytical services for physicochemical and ADME properties for early drug discovery markets. Adapting gold standard methods for compatibility with early drug discovery (throughput, sample requirements, turnaround time, and cost), Analiza developed the first automated, miniaturized, shake flask system for LogD in 1999. Since 2005, Analiza has provided over 150,000 solubility measurements, 45,000 LogD measurements and 2,500 pKa measurements. Analiza extends the in-house physchem and ADME profiling capabilities of small and large pharma and biotech alike.

Name: DemeRx
Description: Welcome to DemeRx. We are a pioneering clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company driven by a steadfast commitment to transform addiction therapeutics and improve outcomes for individuals battling substance use disorders. Our focus is on developing DMX-1001 (oral noribogaine), a promising investigational neuroplastogen for alcohol use disorder, which affects over 29 million people in the U.S.

Name: Amplexd Therapeutics
Description: Amplexd Therapeutics is on a mission to develop accessible, non-invasive treatments for HPV-induced cervical dysplasia.

Name: Vaccine Production Program/VRC/NIAID/NIH
Description: The mission of VPP is to facilitate the development of effective vaccines for human infectious disease and outbreaks. This includes a comprehensive program of research on the NIH intramural campus, work with scientists in academic and industrial laboratories, efficient translation from research into vaccines materials for clinical trials and licensure by partners through NIH. Since its inception in 2001, the VPP has overseen the manufacture of 40 different vaccine products for HIV, influenza, filoviruses (Ebola and Marburg), and alphaviruses (chikungunya, SARS, and West Nile).

Name: BioExcel LLC
Description:
BioExcel provides strategic guidance to biotech startups to obtain non-dilutive funding while preserving owner equity. 
BioExcel believes in aiding entrepreneurs increase time available for innovation toward the goal of commercialization.
BioExcel is driven to help you leap forward on the path of commercialization. Our experience and project management skills combine to bring measurable outcomes.  
We are a team of biotech and pharma executives specializing in non-dilutive funding and biomedical commercialization.  We bring extensive experience in venture investments, commercialization strategy, product development, and fundraising.  Being involved in numerous product development startups, we have successfully negotiated the "Valley of Death" with non-dilutive funding strategies spanning multiple therapeutic areas.

Name: MDNA Life Sciences
Description: We are an innovative life sciences company focused on the development of liquid biopsy tests based on the mitochondrial genome. We have discovered novel biomarkers and designed laboratory assays, which we refer to as our Mitomic Technology, that are intended to use mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) to detect cancer earlier, more accurately, and less invasively than traditional methods. Though further technical development and clinical validation is required to determine efficacy in multiple diseases and disease states, our management believes that the unique structural and functional characteristics of mtDNA, and more specifically mutated mtDNA, make mtDNA a biological system for biomarker identification, early disease detection, monitoring, risk assessment, and therapeutic targeting.
Location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States

Name: Dignify Therapeutics
Description: Developer of novel drug therapies intended to restore voluntary control of excretory function to neurologically impaired people. The company provides effective and convenient pharmaceutical agents that trigger the voiding of bladder and bowel contents when the person wishes, enabling patients with spinal cord injury, spina bifida, and other neurological conditions to have an enhanced way of life.

Name: Anatrace
Description:
Research facilities, academic institutions and industrial customers worldwide have trusted Anatrace for high-purity detergents, lipids, customs and, of course, higher standards since  the late 1980's.  Once again a privately owned business, we’re now setting those standards higher than ever before.

Well regarded as top performers for membrane protein structural biology, Anatrace products are chosen for their uniquely pure molecules – and the exacting chemistry behind them. From compounds designed to disrupt cell membranes to products that stabilize or solubilize unstable macromolecules and proteins, we’re always raising the bar. So your structural studies, functional biology work, or chemical synthesis project will yield incredibly reliable results.

Along with our vast portfolio of products, our chemists can develop specialized solutions tailored to meet your unique specifications. We can also provide custom synthesis services and expert analytical work to aid your own research and development team. The possibilities are limitless – just like the levels of perfection we reach for.

Name: MEDNA Scientific
Description: MEDNA Scientific is a health tech company developing informatics and robotics for healthcare applications.

Name: RESTEM
Description: RESTEM is a leading clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing off-the-shelf, next-generation cell therapies designed to modulate the immune system. Leveraging our proprietary products, robust clinical development expertise, and cutting-edge-manufacturing capabilities, we advance two potentially groundbreaking programs, umbilical cord lining stem cells (ULSCs) for auto-immune diseases and natural killer cell (NK) therapeutics targeting senescence and age-associated disorders.  Our therapies are intended to treat a broad range of disabling diseases and are designed to improve patient outcomes, as well as overall health and wellness. RESTEM is headquartered in Miami, Florida.

Name: Cenetron Diagnostics
Description:
Clinical trials demand logistics that get it right the first time, on time, every time. With over 20 years of experience and hundreds of completed clinical trials worldwide, Cenetron, part of Versiti Clinical Trials, is your end-to-end clinical trial management partner. 

In addition to offering industry leading central laboratory services, Cenetron provides custom solutions tailored to fit each trial's unique parameters. With 24 hour turnaround time for custom specimen collection kits, standard next day domestic shipping, 1-3 day international shipping, and same day pull and ship for stored samples, Cenetron lends unparalleled speed, efficiency, and quality to your clinical trial. Our experienced and dedicated clinical trial consultants work with your team to support your research goals through every phase, every day.

Cenetron specializes in molecular diagnostics, and has supported pivotal global trials for HCV, HIV, and HBV drug development programs. A full offering of safety testing, including hematology, chemistry, and immunology testing is offered at Cenetron.

Services & Technology
- Central laboratory services
- Custom assay development and companion diagnostic tests
- Custom specimen collection kits with online ordering and tracking
- Trial site support
- Project management
- Sample ConciergeTM
- Custom laboratory report programming
- 24/7 access to real time study data through GlobeSync
- Clinical data management
- Custom data transfers and alerts
- Customized labels
- Shipping logistics
- Expansive test menu now including specialty testing by Versiti

Name: Resonant Therapeutics
Description: The Resonant platform generates antibodies to targets which other technologies have missed and cutting years off the discovery process.

Name: MassTech Inc.
Description:
MassTech Inc., located at 6992 Columbia Gateway Drive, Suite 160, Columbia, Maryland USA, (formerly Mass Technologies, Burtonsville Maryland) is a privately owned analytical instrumentation and technology company incorporated in 2001 for developing AP MALDI, field deployable ion trap mass spectrometer, and conducting on-going research and development in support of product lines.

MassTech is the only licensed manufacturer of AP MALDI ion sources. MassTech’s AP MALDI ion source product has been adapted to commercial mass spectrometers from major equipment manufacturers: Agilent, Sciex, Bruker Daltonics, JEOL, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Waters, for both OEM and direct sales around the world.

MassTech’s new MT Explorer 30 ion trap mass spectrometer offers desktop performance in a transportable package, has customizable software, and has potential for a variety of applications. Its compact design is ideal for field use and its MSn capability is great for structure elucidations and chemical and biological identifications.

Name: Revibe Technologies
Description: Revibe Technologies is dedicated to helping children and adults overcome obstacles faced in the classroom and workplace by fusing psychology with technology. School psychologist Rich Brancaccio founded Revibe in 2013 to create a specialized tool to help kids overcome their difficulties by leveling the playing field through technology. Revibe is a wearable that leverages proprietary algorithms to help kids adults combat distraction through gentle vibration reminders.
Location: Wake Forest, North Carolina, United States

Name: SPIMA Therapeutics
Description:
SPIMA Therapeutics emerges as a spin-off from the University of Montpellier, France, uniting experts in cutting-edge peptide chemistry and inflammation biology.

SPIMA focuses on developing innovative peptide-based immunotherapies for challenging targets, particularly protein-protein interactions. Our lead program is a Stapled Peptide targeting the Myddosome complex. This innovative approach holds immense promise for revolutionizing treatments in inflammatory and oncological diseases, offering hope where it's needed most.
SPIMA Therapeutics is part of the nexus of Landmark Bioventures.

Join us in shaping the future of medicine, where discovery meets dedication.

Name: International Congress for Ataxia Research (ICAR)
Description: This Congress will combine the best of our organizations’ popular research meetings, including NAF’s Ataxia Investigators Meeting (AIM) and the International Ataxia Research Conference (IARC), co-led by FARA, Ataxia UK, GoFAR, and other partner organizations. ICAR 2022 will include plenary sessions, poster sessions, breakouts and workshops. Featured topics include: gene discovery, disease mechanisms, cerebellar non-motor circuits and functions, emerging and existing therapeutics, biomarkers and late breaking research. ICAR will also feature workshops with practical demonstrations, discussions on challenges of new and established technologies, and sessions specifically designed by and for junior investigators.

Name: Parion Sciences
Description: Parion Sciences is a development stage company dedicated to research, development, and commercialization of treatments to restore patient’s innate mucosal surface defenses.  In the eye and in the lung, our layer of protective mucus plays an important role in keeping our bodies healthy. Sometimes though, either through genetics, aging or environmental stimulus, our innate mucosal defense system can become compromised. Parion’s science driven technologies target respiratory and ocular diseases in which the patient’s ability to protect their mucosal surfaces is compromised.

Name: To Cure A Rose Foundation
Description:
To Cure A Rose Foundation was founded by Casey McPherson, when he discovered his daughter Rose had a rare disease with no cure. 

200 million children suffer from rare genetic diseases, and only 5% of those disease's have a therapeutic option. 30% of those children will die before their 5th birthday. Yesterday, most of these diseases would have cost hundreds of millions of dollars and over a decade to solve. Today, we have the technology to cure many of these diseases, but we don't have the funding, business models, pipelines, and efficiencies needed to do this at scale. To Cure A Rose Foundation is laser focused on creating a pathway for these children by revolutionizing the drug development process. 

We rely on the support of generous donors - large and small, to fund the life changing work we do. Please reach out if you'd like to become apart of To Cure A Rose Foundation.

Name: Lamassu BioTech
Description:
Lamassu Biotech is a private, clinical stage biopharmaceutical company that uses innovative processes to speed up the development of transformational treatments for humans and animals. Lamassu’s patient-centric approach to research and drug development focuses on making advancements that address unmet needs with novel and targeted strategies, ensuring greater efficiency and shorter approval timeframes. 
The company is pioneering a genetically targeted novel therapeutic to combat locally advanced metastatic p53 wild-type tumors, using SA53 (Selective Activator of p53) to targets the MDM2 protein, a key regulator of the tumor suppressor p53 gene. SA53 has earned investigational new drug application (IND) approval from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and is currently undergoing Phase 1/2a clinical trials at Cleveland Clinic.
Lamassu is also advancing a novel small molecule therapy for acute pancreatitis, RABI-767, which was developed at by leading scientists Mayo Clinic. The drug has shown profound efficacy to completely mitigate mortality and morbidity and is currently undergoing Phase II clinical trial in partnership with Arrivo BioVentures. 
Lamassu Pets, the veterinary division of Lamassu Biotech, is collaborating with The Ohio State University to advance a National Institutes of Health (NIH)-funded clinical trial of canine RABI-767, a novel therapeutic targeting acute pancreatitis in dogs. Canine acute pancreatitis (CAP) is a life-threatening condition that currently has no effective treatments in veterinary medicine.

Name: Clyra Medical Technologies
Description:
Clyra Medical Technologies, founded on our mission of “Make Lives Better”, is a healthcare company that develops and commercializes products designed to safely treat wound and skin infections and promote wound healing, while reducing the need for antibiotics.

Clyra Medical Technologies products feature a potent and broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal & antiviral oxidation system.  With no known acquired resistance capability we deliver it on demand and in a proper dose so that it is safe and effective.

Name: BioLabs North Carolina
Description: BioLabs North Carolina is a unique biotech coworking facility in downtown Durham, North Carolina. Our aim is to attract the most ambitious startup companies in life sciences. This premium open lab space and office space favors collaboration. The lab is equipped with top-of-the-line research equipment, with additional services to help resident companies reach their milestones faster on less capital.

Name: Tract Bio
Description:
Tract Bio is a biotechnology company focused on discovering and developing novel therapies to
transform the treatment of cancer and inflammatory disease. Tract’s proprietary line of FAP-activated peptide drug conjugates (PDCs) uses advanced targeting technology to enhance the safety and efficacy of cancer therapeutics. The Company has developed FAP-activated PDC versions of multiple oncology drugs that Tract scientists have shown are effective against various forms of epithelial cancers. Coupled with Tract Bio’s breakthrough stem-cell based platform, stemEchoTM, which allows Tract to clone the epithelial stem cells that drive the growth of cancer and inflammation, the company has the potential to lead powerful advances in the treatment of highly prevalent cancers and inflammatory diseases, including esophageal, lung, pancreatic, ovarian and gastric cancer, as well as COPD, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, cystic fibrosis and Crohn's disease.

Name: Center for Genomic and Computational Biology (GCB), Duke University
Description:
GCB is an interdisciplinary center where faculty from across Duke University’s campus collaborate to study complex problems in genomic and computational biology, train researchers, and develop genomic technologies.

GCB's mission is to foster excellence in genomics and computational biology across Duke’s campus. GCB researchers do this through research collaborations, educational activities, and core facilities. GCB is passionate about interdisciplinary research that dissolves the distinction between the wet lab and quantitative analysis. GCB is also dedicated to training the current and next generation of researchers through educational programs that support undergraduates, graduate students, and senior researchers with a variety of classes, hands-on workshops, and research opportunities. In addition, GCB operates six core facilities that develop and disseminate next-generation technologies and best practices for research in genomic and computational biology.

Name: Kiniciti
Description:
Kiniciti is a new Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe platform established to partner with companies that have the potential to transform the cell and gene therapy ecosystem and deliver the promise of these therapies to impact patients’ lives.

Bringing novel treatments to the patients who need them most — in an economically viable way — is too often crippled by persistent bottlenecks, constraints and inefficiencies in the development, manufacturing and delivery of those innovations.

At Kiniciti, our imperative is to make the promise of breakthrough CGT therapies a reality, so that future treatments reach patients as quickly and cost-efficiently as possible. There can’t be a tradeoff between scientific advancements and patients’ access to life-changing therapies; both must be addressed simultaneously.

Kiniciti is focused on investing in opportunities with the potential to leverage technology and capabilities that can help drive transformational change and ensure the promise of CGT therapeutics is delivered to patients in need. 

So we’re ready and able to pursue partnerships in:
• Cell sources and other enabling quality- controlled starting and raw materials
• Enabling technology platforms (including cell-programming and gene- editing innovations)
• Key tools, services and enablers for process development and scale-up
• Innovations and solutions from source-to-patient delivery
• Other solutions designed to fulfill the promise of breakthrough treatments while concurrently reducing costs to ensure affordable access for patients

In forming Kiniciti, Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe (WCAS) hand-selected leading life sciences executives and committed a minimum of $250M to support companies primed to transform healthcare through their CGT offerings. While control-stake investments are part of our WCAS pedigree and our preference when appropriate, Kiniciti has a flexible remit to ensure that we invest in the right companies, with the right technology, at the right time.

Name: Halo Health Systems
Description:
Halo Health is a digital platform that accelerates clinical trials for pharma. Our solution offers telemedicine, remote patient monitoring, patient engagement apps and workflow automation. The solution minimizes clinical site visits, increases quality and access to data and reduces cost. Our platform supports both hybrid and decentralized trials. 

Halo Health harnesses Internet of Things (IoT), Mobile and AI technologies to provide SaaS based solution for clinical trials.

A Health Wildcatter & Capital Factory company

Name: Ilex Life Sciences LLC
Description: Your source for novel and high quality laboratory reagents for life sciences research.

Name: I.W. Tremont Co., Inc.
Description: I.W. Tremont Co., Inc. founded in 1979 serves laboratory distributors, analytical instrument manufacturers, IVD, medical device manufacturers and technical markets as a private label and OEM supplier of filter media. Product focus is glass microfiber, extraction thimbles, syringe filters, cellulose papers, membranes and technical specialty materials. Unique product lines include high purity porous materials used in filtration, wicking, and conveyance applications of powders and liquids.  ISO9001:2008 registered with TUV Rheinland and GMP compliant. High level customer service and confidentiality is assured.

Name: MOLTOX
Description:
Founded in Maryland and later settled in the beautiful Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina, since 1986 MOLTOXTM has been and continues to be a leading manufacturer of products used in Genetic Toxicology, Industrial Microbiology, Environmental Biology and Molecular Biology.  Through the dedication and commitment of our longstanding team, we have assisted customers around the world in their pursuit of testing, research and development in each of these fields.   Our customers have come to rely on the  MOLTOXTM  name for our high quality products and continued commitment to facilitate their work now and in the future.
MOLTOXTM manufactures products used in mutagenicity tests. Our products and services for human risk assessment include MOLTOXTM minimal glucose agar plates, top agars, Salmonella and E. coli tester strains, frozen and lyophilized S9, MUTAZYMETM, NADPH-regenerating systems and positive control chemicals and are distributed worldwide.  MOLTOXTM  offers Salmonella and E. coli test kits in plate incorporation and fluctuation test formats.  We also provide our SOS/UMU assay kit, which is designed for use with solid and aqueous environmental samples.
MOLTOXTM   is also a well respected manufacturer of  prepared bacteriological media including nutrient, selective and enrichment media used in industrial, environmental and molecular microbiology.   MOLTOXTM observes the highest standards in the production and packaging of prepared media.

Name: Cell Bridge Strategies, LLC
Description: Cell Bridge Strategies, LLC is a global growth consulting firm that helps executives and investors in life sciences, regenerative medicine, cell, and the cell-gene therapies. Cell Bridge Strategies has the deep understanding of the technologies, products, global regulatory environments, markets, operations, and US and international growth opportunities to help companies advance their products, increase valuation, build and grow revenue streams. Cell Bridge Strategies delivers insights that  help companies match their core assets to the optimal growth opportunities. Our comprehensive consulting process spans R&D, clinical, regulatory, and commercialization.

Name: BaneBio
Description:
BaneBio is a provider of laboratory equipment, supplies, and services to the global scientific community.  We provide high quality, gently-used laboratory equipment that has been quality tested and re-commissioned for sale. All our equipment includes our standard 90-day warranty.  

A competitive price is not the only reason our customers buy from us. BaneBio also assists its customers with financing options, equipment acquisition, equipment consulting, equipment repair and testing, and manufacturer's certification as well as appraisals and logistics management. In addition, we have the ability to provide other ancillary products and services as required by our customers. 

Founded in 2008, BaneBio is continuously striving to build our customer base by treating customers respectfully, taking the time to ensure our products meet our stringent quality control standards and providing high-quality certified products at surplus prices. Our customer base ranges from start-ups to large biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, colleges and universities, medical schools and hospitals and clinics.  

Based in Frederick, MD – a few miles outside Montgomery County, the epicenter for biotechnology in the Mid-Atlantic Region -- our strategic location provides a hub to other biotechnological hot-spots, with direct access to Baltimore, Washington D.C., and Northern Virginia.

Name: Advanced Biotechnologies Inc
Description:
As a leading international supplier of viral reagents, Advanced Biotechnologies has spent more than 35 years perfecting a process for creating large lots of the purest, most concentrated reagents available - from common strains to extremely rare products no other manufacturer can supply. Our products have reduced non-specific reactivity so if, for instance, you need to optimize an assay against a particular virus you can count on getting the native components of that virus, & nothing else. 

We manufacture on site in our own custom-designed facility, so we know exactly what goes into our products, & we carefully control every step of the process. We also perform QC testing after a freeze-thaw cycle, so you can be sure that we're analyzing exactly what you're getting.

In addition to the diverse collection of products listed in our catalog, our skilled research team delivers outstanding results on custom projects & TEM services.  

We are committed to our clients’ success as we continually innovate our technologies, production techniques, & quality control measures.

Name: Homebiogas Kenya
Description:
At Home Biogas Kenya, we constructs all biogas plant types ( fixed dome & flexible plants) and waste processing plants.
Home biogas also supplies biogas appliances such as Biogas double cooker (stove), single cooker, commercial cooker, biogas lamp, room heater, water heater, fixed dome plants, portable biogas plants, gas storage bags, gas pump, slurry pump, flow meter, pressure gauge, desulphuriser pellets, biogas fridge, biogas generator etc

Our plants have an excellent reputation for quality, high availability and reliability, for which they are valued by operators and financiers alike.

We offer solutions for domestic, medium and commercial clients.
Other Services
1. Conducting feasibility studies
2. Planning and installation of solar products
3. Connecting energy developers with financiers/investors
4. Energy co-generation.
5. Research and Consulting
6. Supply of other renewable energy technologies such as solar, wind and hydro.

Name: Center for Drug Discovery (CDD)
Description:
The Center for Drug Discovery is a strategic center and resource for investigators at Baylor College of Medicine and beyond. The CDD quickly identifies and advances small molecules to clinical trials, with the goal of developing cost-effective, novel drug and treatment options. The CDD is devoted to finding new cures for a wide range of diseases, including infectious diseases, neurological diseases, metabolic disorders, cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and inflammatory disorders. Its mission is to develop small molecule probes, preclinical candidates and drugs for researchers and clinicians in the Texas Medical Center and beyond. Though based at Baylor, CDD members include faculty at other institutions in the Texas Medical Center, most notably Texas Children’s Hospital and The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.

The CDD bridges the gap between academic research and pharmaceutical discovery and provides researchers with an economically viable entry into early-stage drug discovery as well as enable the study and validation of protein targets and disease mechanisms. The CDD uses state-of-the-art equipment and methodologies that will yield better candidate compounds for drugs and experimental therapeutics.

The center employs techniques that sample more fully the theoretical total “chemical space” that comprises all possible chemical synthesis reaction products, resulting in compounds that more efficiently fill three-dimensional molecular space and better modulate the functions of specific target proteins. Chief among these methods are DNA-encoded chemistry technology and fragment-based library discovery that will lower the cost of drug discovery, speed up the process and bring new hope to finding cures for some of the most urgent diseases that afflict human populations.

To date, the CDD has produced libraries of compounds (now totaling over four billion compounds) that will translate into new leads, commercial opportunities, and licensure. The ul

Name: Integrative Sciences Initiative
Description:
The incredible advances in molecular innovation over the last century have undeniably shaped our world for the better—saving lives, increasing crop yields, and improving living standards. However, these achievements come with significant challenges that demand our immediate attention. As antibiotic resistance rises, environmental damage from agrochemicals accumulates, and some medicines pose new health risks, we cannot afford to ignore the consequences of these innovations. The next wave of scientific breakthroughs must not only solve pressing problems but also ensure a safer, more sustainable future. This is a pivotal moment for action—one where research, innovation, and training must be focused on creating solutions that protect both people and the planet.

NC State University has a deep history of delivering impactful, real-world solutions for some of society's grandest challenges. Through the launch of the Integrative Sciences Initiative and its home, Woodson Hall, NC State is positioned to cement itself as an international hub for accelerated molecular innovation. Woodson Hall will be a central location for researchers and students from across campus to join together around shared projects and will connect existing centers of excellence on campus.  Core training and research efforts will be enabled by chemistry, biochemistry, engineering, physics, and textiles but will be empowered by collaborations ranging from the humanities and social sciences to design and the arts. Industry partners are engaged in both training and research, and a focus on innovation, entrepreneurship, and commercialization is embedded in all aspects of the program.

Name: Metaclipse Therapeutics Corporation
Description: Metaclipse Therapeutics is a clinical stage biotech company developing next-generation immunotherapies to treat cancer & vaccines to prevent infectious diseases using our proprietary biological adjuvants. Our personalized immunotherapy platform, MembrexTM, has demonstrated promising preclinical data across multiple solid tumors with Phase 1 clinical trials for triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) and head and neck cancer (HNSCC) underway. We are committed to continuous innovation using biological adjuvants for therapeutic and preventative vaccines.

Name: Clongen Laboratories, LLC
Description: Clongen Laboratories has two main branches: a CLIA-certified Clinical Molecular Diagnostics Laboratory and a Contract Research Laboratory.   The laboratory is also FDA certified for handling medical devices as well as human derived fluids and tissues.  We specialize in infectious agent testing using PCR and Real-Time PCR.

Name: NeuroTherapia, Inc.
Description:
NeuroTherpia, Inc., founded in 2015 by Drs. Mohamed Naguib and Joseph Foss, is developing new therapies for diseases with an underlying component of neuroinflammation. Initial research has led to the development of our lead compound NTRX-07. NTRX-07 (previously known as MDA7) which has been shown to decrease activation of microglial cells in the brain. Decreasing activation of these cells leads to decreased inflammation and decreased injury to surrounding nerve cells. Decreasing this inflammation can treat and even prevent the development of neuropathic pain in settings of nerve injury or chemotherapy. Recent work has shown that blocking this inflammation is also important in reversing the effects seen in Alzheimer's Disease (AD).

We have completed initial Phase 1 safety trials of NTRX-07 in volunteers and are planning to do a  Phase 2 trial in patients with AD in 2025.

Tony Giordano, Ph.D. is the CEO for NeuroTherapia. He is a serial entrepreneur who brings his extensive research background in AD and business experience to the company.

Joseph Foss, M.D., has over 30 years experience in translational clinical pharmacology, and has led successful drug development programs in academia and industry.

Marianna Kiraly, Ph.D. is the VP for Research and Development.
Marianna has over 15 years of experience in research, data analysis and education at academic institutions and corporations. Before joining NeuroTherapia she served as the Neuroscience Lead for Switch Therapeutics.

Name: EQO
Description:
Curious about what's living in your lake, river, wetland, or marine ecosystem? 

eDNA and eRNA can be used to detect and understand invasive, endangered, and microbiological aquatic species to support biodiversity, public health & safety, as well as commercial interests tied to a specific surface water asset.  

As a lab, we are experts in environmental genomics and transcriptomics, helping you understand the presence and activity of species and population dynamics in your aquatic ecosystem

Name: Durin Life Sciences Inc.
Description: We’re a biotechnology company dedicated to improving early detection of complex diseases through our innovative DuritectTM tests.

Name: FlowTex
Description:
Welcome to the FlowTex flow cytometry user group, a forum for information and networking for the flow cytometry labs and users of Texas and the surrounding area.


The mission of FlowTex is to provide a forum for education and discussion regarding flow cytometry and related topics. We encourage questions, technical discussions and hold educational workshops, lectures, seminars, and the annual FlowTex Conference. Based in the Texas Medical Center, Houston TX, FlowTex is an associated society of ISAC (International Society for the Advancement of Cytometry). Our goal is to promote and foster research through the sharing of information and experiences in flow cytometry.

Name: Antigenix Therapeutics
Description:
Antigenix Therapeutics is a biotechnology company dedicated to giving cancer patients more hope and more choices. We are developing novel antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapies for cancers resistant to current treatments.


www.antigenixthera.com

Name: Invivotek
Description:
Invivotek,  a Genesis Drug Discovery and Development (GD3) Company, is a global pre-clinical contract research organization (CRO)  specializing in small animal studies for drug discovery and early optimization.  Invivotek's facility was opened in 2012 and our first commercial project launched in 2013. 

Invivotek offers both custom and standard pre-clinical services for drug discovery and development programs for our clients. Invivotek’s portfolio includes animal models and bioassays designed to support in vivo testing of compounds related to Immunology and Inflammation, Oncology,  Metabolic, and Cardiovascular diseases.  Invivotek’s in vivo testing capabilities are supported by biochemical and molecular biology techniques as well as functional assays with primary cell cultures established from various mouse tissues under disease model and normal conditions. These assays provide tools to study the mechanism of action of various test therapeutics or potential target genes and to explore drug efficacy biomarkers.  The collective experience across multiple therapeutic areas in conjunction with the business and project management skills of the team working in a state-of-the-art animal facility, position Invivotek as a leading provider of preclinical in vivo services.

Name: Chemyx, Inc.
Description:
Chemyx Inc. is a global manufacturer of high-precision syringe pumps for use in the life science, chemical research, and analytical equipment industries. Additional OEM services and custom-built fluid delivery tools are provided by a team of in-house engineers for specialized applications, meeting almost any research requirement at the highest standard of excellence.
 
A leader in innovation, Chemyx was the first company to develop the next-generation syringe pump with an interactive LCD interface and integrated syringe database in early 2000. Today, Chemyx continues to push advancements in the laboratory services industry and is trusted among thousands of scientists who depend on the durability, value, and precision of our products. From microfluidics and mass spectrometry to aerospace and energy research, Chemyx is the standard for high-precision fluid delivery.

Name: BioLum Sciences
Description:
Leveraging biomarker analysis with an integrated approach, BioLum is transforming precision medicine and early disease detection. Our highly-sensitive, selective assays, diagnostics, and lab services provide insights for more efficient therapeutic R&D.

With a focus on reactive oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur species (RONSS), BioLum's assays outperform gold standards (including Griess & DAF). Our advanced chemiluminescence improves signal-to-noise by eliminating background autofluorescence, ensuring superior accuracy and precision with broad specimen compatibility.

We work with pharmaceutical companies and researchers through preclinical discovery and development. To optimize treatment efficacy in complex diseases, it's critical to have a deep understanding of signaling pathways, mechanisms of action, and cellular interactions. 

Capabilities and services:
-biomarker analysis
-compound library screening
-efficacy testing
-rapid evaluation methods
-custom assay synthesis
-small molecule synthesis
-drug repurposing
-quantitative and qualitative insights
-early target identification and validation
-ADME
-dose dependency testing
-in vitro analysis
-PK/PD
-formula optimization 
-probe synthesis and development

Clearly, more sustainable, domestically available, and rapidly scalable alternative sources and approaches are needed to fill the predicted shortfalls.  Hevea rubber is handled and marked-up many times (as many as 29) before an end-product is produced.  EnergyEne expects to limit the product handling (from farm to end product) to less than five intermediaries.

Name: Protein Capture Science
Description:
Unmet Need:
There is an unmet need for a single-column, universal platform method to reliably purify tagless recombinant proteins. Affinity tag methods followed by tag removal, although commonly used, are unreliable, complex, lead to productivity losses in research, and are impractical for biopharmaceutical production.

Solution:
The key capabilities and advantages of the novel technology for protein purification provided by Protein Capture Science are:
1. Provides tagless purified proteins via tag self-cleavage during affinity purification
2. Gentle cleaving based on small pH change
3. Reproducible purity and recovery of target
4. Tunable target-independent cleavage rate
5. Scalable from laboratory to manufacturing
6. Simple and inexpensive buffer requirements
7. Opportunity to merge multi-platform processes into one platform (from R&D to production)

Product:
Intein-based product is a resin containing proprietary intein-based fragment that allows traceless and tagless self-cleaving protein purification.  Two forms of product are available to purchase:
1.  A kit containing pre-packed column (1mL or 5 mL)
2. A bulk resin (10 mL to L scales)

Built upon discoveries from the University of Cincinnati and Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, Preservation Bio was formed to address the global platelet shortage caused by decreasing donations and supply waste due to the short shelf life of donated platelets that must currently be stored at room temperature. The company has secured the rights to this cutting-edge technology directly from renowned academic investigators, Dr. Jose Cancelas and Dr. Yi Zheng, who serve as the scientific co-founders of Preservation Bio and are widely regarded as leading authorities in the field of transfusion medicine.

Dr. Cancelas, a distinguished expert in transfusion medicine, and Dr. Zheng, an expert in RhoA biochemistry, led the pioneering research efforts at the University of Cincinnati and Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, laying the groundwork for Preservation Bio’s innovative platelet storage solution. They have played a pivotal role in advancing Preservation Bio’s mission to improve patient outcomes and revolutionize the platelet donation storage process. The company’s ex vivo additive protects platelets from the damage normally caused by cold temperatures,allowing them to be stored in the refrigerator. This represents a commercial opportunity that will benefit both hospitals and cancer clinics and their patients.

Preservation Bio’s product is designed to be added to bags of donated platelets, allowing them to be refrigerated and extending their shelf life from the current 5-7 days up to 14 days or possibly longer. This could significantly reduce the number of platelets that are discarded each year due to expiration (currently 10-15%).

If you had an orthopedic problem, you could get a shot of Cortisone, but that wouldn't really fix the underlying problem.  A better option would be for your doctor to prepare some of your blood or tissue using the Reviticell System to create your treatment.

This non-pharmaceutical approach for treating you is called regenerative medicine and it's driving a huge emerging market.  In fact, even in its infancy, it's more than a 50 billion-dollar industry.

What's unique about regenerative medicine is that, not only do doctors have to treat their patients, but, first, they have to prepare their patients' treatments, while they are under anesthesia and laying there waiting.  As you can imagine, this adds a level of complexity to what's already going on in the operating room, not to mention significant risk to the patient as the clock continues to tick.

Worse yet, doctors who practice regenerative medicine are completely dissatisfied because, until now, there hasn’t been a single medical-device they can use to efficiently prepare regenerative treatments with consistent and effective outcomes.

Unlike the inferior devices currently being marketed, the patented Reviticell System enables the efficient and precise preparation of regenerative treatments, because it's configured with a sequence of modular cartridges that each contain the exact components necessary to prepare a specific medical treatment, in accordance with a proprietary protocol.  This is what makes producing consistent and effective outcomes possible.

Name: Convergence Institute at Johns Hopkins University
Description:
The Convergence Institute at the Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine (SKCCC) aims to leverage multi-disciplinary team science to solve a problem: cancer. 
 
The past decade witnessed exponential advances to cellular and molecular profiling technologies, artificial intelligence, and cancer therapeutics. These new and innovative techniques for understanding the biology of many cancers have yet to be translated into in-human studies to advance the treatment of advanced cancer. 
 
In medicine, convergence is defined as the integration of life sciences, physical sciences, engineering sciences, and information sciences. At SKCCC, the Convergence Institute is where doctors, nurses, astronomers, atmospheric scientists, engineers, computer scientists, physicists, bioethicists, biologists, materials scientists, and mathematicians work side by side to apply the convergence of their knowledge. Experts from all disciplines and specialties must work together to invent technologies; create the algorithms; develop safer, less invasive, and more effective ways to prevent, detect and treat cancers; and overcome the metastatic barrier, converting even advanced cancers to chronic or curable diseases. 
 
Our mission is to accelerate progress in the fight against cancer by building, training, and catalyzing convergence teams who will utilize their diverse scientific disciplines and technologies to foster innovation. We believe that these teams will discover and develop new and more successful ways to treat and prevent cancer. We will support this mission by developing new technologies for first-in-human research, funding pilot studies, by creating new training programs for graduate students, postdocs, and by offering innovative education opportunities for faculty and staff. 

The Institute leadership blends translational cancer research and computational biology with co-Directors Dr. Elizabeth Jaffee and Dr. Elana Fertig.

RethinkBronchiectasis.com by Insmed Incorporated is a source of information and resources on bronchiectasis for healthcare professionals.

Bronchiectasis is a chronic and progressive disease usually marked by permanent, abnormal dilation and persistent inflammation of the airways. There have long been unmet needs in bronchiectasis, though it affects approximately 450,000 people in the United States and more globally.

Bronchiectasis is commonly associated with symptoms of chronic cough, daily sputum production, and recurrent infections. It initially presents with nonspecific symptoms that mimic more common conditions such as COPD or asthma, which experts believe often delays diagnosis or leads to misdiagnoses. Bronchiectasis also notably causes exacerbations in which patients experience the worsening of multiple symptoms, requiring a change in treatment. 
 
To disrupt the vicious vortex of disease progression, a comprehensive management approach is required, focusing on all 4 primary drivers of the disease: addressing chronic airway infection, reducing chronic airway inflammation—primarily neutrophilic, enhancing mucociliary clearance, and preventing further lung destruction.

For more information about managing and treating bronchiectasis, visit RethinkBronchiectasis.com.

HCell Granted Orphan Drug Designation from the U.S. FDA for HC017AA Alopecia Areata in the Pediatric Population

Austin, Texas – December 22, 2017 – HCell Inc., a privately held biotechnology company based in Austin, Texas, focusing on Alopecia Areata in the Pediatric Population, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) to HC017AA for the treatment of pediatric patients with alopecia areata, a devastating hair loss disease. 

“The granting of Orphan Drug status by the U.S. FDA is a significant milestone for HCell in the HC017AA development program,” said Jaehyun Lim M.D., Ph.D, co-founder and Chief Science Officer at HCell Inc. “We are working diligently to get ready to conduct the clinical study for this significant, yet unmet, medical need for alopecia areata in pediatric patients.” 

The FDA grants Orphan Drug Designation status to drugs and biologics that treat rare diseases, which is defined as those affecting fewer than 200,000 people, in the U.S. The FDA Office of Orphan Products Development evaluates scientific and clinical data submissions from sponsors to identify and designate products as promising for rare diseases and to advance scientific development of such promising medical products. 

“ODD from the FDA’s recognition gives HCell Inc. a number of potential financial benefits and is aligned with our ongoing work seeking expedited pathways towards product approval in the U.S.,” Dr. Lim added.

HCell Inc. is also working on initiating regulatory steps for HC0100, which comprises proprietary composition and procedure for the treatment of Androgenic Alopecia conditions in both men and women. Further, HCell Inc. is planning pre-clinical development with the intent to launch a human clinical study in the U.S.

For more information, visit www.hcell.net.

Generation Biotech, based in Princeton, NJ, provides kits and services for nucleic acid analysis and viral screening.  Our kits are for research use only (RUO) and not approved for diagnostic use.  

Omicron-specific VoXcreen and VoXident PCR kits for SARS-Cov-2 variant of concern screening were developed by our partner GenXPro in Frankfurt, Germany. Their competitive advantage is detecting and identifying SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VoCs) in one single step. Doing so speeds up time from collection to result, cuts the cost per test to about half, simplifies testing workflow and frees up capacity, and significantly reduces the risk of sample mix-ups and errors in reporting test results.  

SmallRNA Ultra Low Input sequencing kits, also developed by GenXPro, are used for the preparation of small RNA libraries to be sequenced on Illumina NGS instruments. The kits require only picogram amounts (0.01 to 500 ng) of total RNA. The entire workflow takes place in a single tube and is gel free, which minimizes losses and increases efficiency:  5-14 fewer PCR cycles than other methods are needed to obtain the minimum for a sequencing lane, and smallRNA sequencing cost can be drastically reduced (50% - 80% vs. others).  The proprietary TrueQuant technology eliminates PCR-derived copies from gene expression data - only the sequence with highest quality of each TrueQuant adapter plus template-sequence combination are maintained.

Experience in single molecule DNA sequencing, single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analysis and transplantation tissue typing led to the development of molecular enrichment and haplotyping methods that utilize magnetic nanoparticles to selectively pull out regions of interest from a complex sample. Genomic segments captured by our RSE and HSE kits are typically 10x longer than fragments isolated by other methods. The user can process the enriched material on her platform of choice for sequencing, quantitative PCR or amplification for other purposes.

Name: Drinkable Air Technologies
Description:
Drinkable Air’s Atmospheric Water Generator Technology (AWG)machines create pure, fresh drinking water out of the air we breathe.

The amount of water vapor in the atmosphere is vast and atmospheric water generation is a technique of harvesting that water vapor to make clean drinking water – the more humidity in the air, the more water that can be produced. Water that is produced by our AWGs is pure, does not contain any contaminants, and represents a method of supplying safe pure water while being environmentally friendly and saving money. Producing water from the air is a sustainable practice through an intelligent use of the most abundant and unlimited supply of water available.

Our AWGs first pull air through an electrostatic-antimicrobial filter, removing air born particles. A condensation unit receives the clean humid airflow and condenses water vapor into liquid. As the machine collects the water, it drops into a collection tank where it is ozonated to keep the water pure and fresh.

In both the C3 and C8 models the water in the tank is chilled then pumped through a series of filters that further purify and then add minerals to the water (Calcium, Magnesium, Carbonates, etc.) to increase and maintain healthy pH levels.

Drinkable Air’s AWG machines run on standard grid electric power but are easily adaptable to sustainable power sources such as wind, solar, solar-wind hybrid and diesel generators. They are well suited for hotel rooms, government facilities, schools, hospitals, offices and residential households and represent a technological breakthrough, creating a way to replace and eliminate plastic water bottles.

Gelatin is obtained by the hydrolysis of collagen which is the principal protein found in skin and 
bones. Fish gelatin is being extracted commercially in Nova Scotia by Kenney & Ross at Port Saxon.
The raw material is the skin from deep water fish such as cod, haddock and pollock, and is obtained 
from local salt fish and frozen skins. The uniqueness of cold water fish gelatin lies in the amino acid 
composition of the gelatin. Although all gelatins are composed of the same 20 amino acids, there can be 
a variation in the amount of amino acids, proline and hydroxyproline. With lower amounts of these 
amino acids, there is less hydrogen bonding of gelatin in water solutions, and hence a reduction in 
the gelling temperature. Gelatin from cod skin gels at 5-10oC, whereas gelatin from carp skin would be 
more similar to animal gelatin, which gels above room temperature. Most people think of gelatin as a 
food additive or part of photographic film. With a lower gelling temperature, other commercial 
applications of cold water fish gelatin have been developed.

Name: CTL-MAT
Description:
Our mission is to enable reliable and ethical drug releases thus reducing unnecessary animal-based testing. 

The Monocyte Activation Test (MAT) is an in-vitro bioassay that detects cytokine release by monocytes contained in human Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) when these are exposed to microbial products.  As opposed to the Limulus Amebocyte Lysate Test (LAL) that detects lipopolysaccharides (LPS) of Gram-negative bacteria only, MAT also detects constituents of Gram-positive bacteria, fungi and viruses. MAT is equally suited for the detection of microbial contaminants as the traditional Rabbit Pyrogen Test (RPT), but avoids the unnecessary reliance on animal testing. Therefore, MAT has evolved as the leading in-vitro alternative to RPT for the mandatory batch release testing of parenteral drugs and medical devices, verifying that they have not been contaminated with microbial products and are safe to administer. The MAT is recommended by the European Pharmacopeia for batch release testing of drugs and medical devices.

Representing a sensitive in-vitro bioassay, successful implementation of MAT critically depends on the availability of fully functional monocytes as indicator cells, optimized and pyrogen-free tissue culture conditions, and a sensitive cytokine detection in the culture supernatant. Our experts are available to perform and interpret test results, including product-specific validation and interference matrices, all while documenting and reporting the test procedure to meet regulatory compliances. CTL-MAT is the only company that can help you with any and all these requirements for performing the MAT at your facility – or we can perform the test for you in our own certified laboratories.

Go Beyond RNA

With the discoveries of novel gene regulatory activities, non-coding RNA classes represent the fundamental biology going beyond coding mRNAs and encoded proteins as the focal point of the central dogma. The pursuit to uncover pivotal roles of ncRNAs in gene regulation, programming, and orchestration has attracted intense scientific interest with alluring opportunities of finding new disease regulators, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. While the industry of gene expression analysis has long been predominantly covering only mRNAs, Arraystar is taking the lead in supporting scientific endeavor into the once hidden yet exciting world of non-coding RNAs: lncRNAs, circular RNAs, microRNAs, tRNAs, tRFs, tiRNAs, snoRNAs and more.

As a newly unveiled layer of gene regulation, epitranscriptomic modifications of coding mRNAs and non-coding RNAs determine the molecular fates and profoundly impact cellular processes, such as RNA activities, splicing, export, stability and translation in disease and health. With rapid advances in the field and new methodology development, epitranscriptomics has come of age. Arraystar is in the best position to help your research into this omics dimension of not only mRNA, but also long and small ncRNA epitranscriptomics.

As a result, bluwatr can help reduce the amount of oily wastes generated at your plant by as much as 80%. And, unlike traditional degreasers that only move oils from one place to another, our products literally transform oils & grease into carbon dioxide & water, eliminating the oils where they are before ever reaching your wastewater disposal systems. And those oils that do enter your oil / water separators can be converted, so they don’t have to be disposed of as non-hazardous wastes. This not only reduces your environmental footprint, but it significantly reduces the costs associated with their disposal.

Our products are completely safe. They are non-toxic, non-pathogenic, & completely harmless to human, plant, animal, and marine life. Protalex’s lead product, PRTX-100, is derived from bacteria that are known to circumvent aspects of the human immune system.

PRTX-100 is a formulation of a proprietary, highly purified form of the Staphylococcal Protein A, which is an immunomodulatory protein produced by Staphylococcus aureus bacteria. PRTX-100 has the ability, at very low concentrations, to bind to human B-lymphocytes and macrophages and to modulate immune processes that mediate inflammation in certain autoimmune diseases. Laboratory studies indicate that the mechanism involves interaction with specific immunologic signaling pathways. Pre-clinical animal studies also demonstrate that very low doses of PRTX-100 have potent therapeutic effects in certain models of immune mediated inflammatory diseases. To date, human clinical studies indicate that PRTX-100 is generally safe and well tolerated at all dose levels evaluated.

Description:
Sentrimed is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company creating safer, orally dosed oncology therapies that target the cancer biomarker podoplanin (PDPN). PDPN is a transmembrane glycoprotein receptor that enables cancer cells to proliferate and migrate. This prognostic biomarker appears early in cancer transformation, persists through malignant progression, and causes poor clinical outcomes. As a result, targeting PDPN could represent an important advancement in the profiling and treatment of cancer.

The Company’s lead product candidate, MASL (lenipagrusin alfa),  is an orally administered therapeutic that targets the PDPN receptor. MASL represents a novel approach to addressing common challenges in oncology treatments that contribute to high recurrence rates and poor patient outcomes. Blocking PDPN by MASL inhibits cancer by altering pathways critical to tumor growth, invasion, evasion and resistance. Additionally, MASL triggers necrotic cell death, which causes host anti-tumor immune responses.

MASL has the potential to treat various stages and types of  cancer, many having large populations of patients with elevated PDPN expression. Research to date shows that MASL is well-tolerated and may be suitable for early and advanced stage cancers. An NIH funded human signal trial was recently completed and published supporting the continued development of MASL. Sentrimed is advancing clinical studies to evaluate MASL as a monotherapy and with standard of care treatments. The Company plans to initially study MASL in head and neck cancer, a disease with high rates of recurrence, limited therapeutic options, and a high prevalence of patients with elevated PDPN.

The more effective delivery of Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles, or BEVs, at lower cost is critical for the advancement of human health. Expora’s mission is to be the global leader in the design and manufacture of BEVs.

The gut has long been regarded as playing a critical role in many vital aspects of human health, including the immune system, brain health, metabolism, and inflammation. “Good” bacteria, aka probiotics, contribute to gut health by producing Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles, or BEVs. BEVs are a newly recognized way the gut microbiome communicates with human cells. These nanosized biological membrane particles are naturally built to survive the harsh conditions of the gastrointestinal tract and deliver concentrated, biologically active cargo—such as nucleic acids, peptides, small molecules, and metabolites—directly to gut tissues, enabling potent, targeted effects. As such, BEVs are an exciting biotech modality to improve human health, and Expora is focused on deploying BEVs for applications in scientific research, consumer health supplements, and therapeutic delivery.

Expora has an unrivaled IP portfolio enabling industrial manufacturing of BEVs at dramatically lower cost (10× cheaper) and far greater consistency, and has the unique ability to modify BEV payloads in order to address specific patient needs. These technologies were invented by Expora’s Co-Founder and CSO, Dr. Nicholas Pirolli, at the University of Maryland. BEVs are not living organisms and are consequently more shelf-stable, and deliver a far higher effective dose to human tissues than is feasible with alternative approaches.

Name: PolarDoc
Description:
PolarDoc is a medical device startup commercializing PPRIM, the Portable Preterm Risk Imaging Monitor — a patented polarimetric imaging system that objectively measures cervical collagen microstructure to assess preterm birth risk. Founded by a team of PhD researchers at Florida International University, PolarDoc bridges cutting-edge optical physics with maternal health diagnostics to address one of the most pressing unmet clinical needs in obstetrics. Today, the frontline tool for assessing cervical readiness is still a physician's fingers. The digital cervical exam, unchanged in its essentials for over sixty years, asks a clinician to palpate the cervix and translate what they feel — soft or firm, effaced or thick — into a subjective score. Two experienced obstetricians examining the same patient minutes apart routinely disagree, and the exam captures nothing about the collagen remodeling that actually precedes preterm labor. It is an assessment of texture, performed by hand, standing in for a measurement of tissue microstructure. PPRIM replaces that judgment call with a five-second, speculum-free optical scan that quantifies what the fingers can only approximate.
Preterm birth is the leading cause of newborn death worldwide, yet no objective, mildly-invasive early-warning tool exists in standard care. PPRIM changes that. Using a speculum-free probe and disposable silicone sheath, PPRIM captures polarimetric images of the cervix and generates a quantitative risk score from early pregnancy, giving clinicians the earliest possible window to intervene before symptoms appear.

Description:
AmeboGenesis's sustainable Amebocyte production process scalably develops bio-identical, high sensitivity Amebocytes - AG-LALTM - that are necessary for the production of LAL for medical endotoxin testing without the need for harvesting horseshoe crab blood. The blood of horseshoe crabs, a source of Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL), is a critical component in ensuring the safety of injectable drugs, vaccines, and implantable devices worldwide. 

The traditional method of obtaining LAL involves the harvesting and bleeding of more than one million horseshoe crabs annually, with a survival rate post-harvest that raises concerns for the Horseshoe Crab’s survival as a species. 

The sustainability, scalability and unique properties of AG-LAL have allowed AmeboGenesisTM to develop AG-RULTM, a biotechnology platform being developed for the rapid detection and potential removal of bacterial endotoxins and inflammatory microbial signals from human fluids, including blood serum and cerebrospinal fluid.

When successfully developed, AG-RUL technologies could enable earlier detection of infection signals and potentially new approaches to managing inflammatory responses associated with sepsis, antimicrobial resistance, and severe bacterial infections. 

What if the future of infection control lies not in killing microbes, but in detecting and neutralizing the molecular signals that make them dangerous?

AG-RUL could be the next era for infection control, beyond antibiotics.

Description:
Asylia Therapeutics is a private development stage biotechnology company committed to transforming scientific advances into safe and effective medicines for cancer and auto-immune diseases.  Founded in 2019 and based in Houston, TX, the company is led by a seasoned team of entrepreneurs, scientific leaders in immunity, oncology and clinical trials, and biotech executives with experience in antibody drug and business development.

Asylia’s lead antibody, ASY-77A, centers on a fundamental mechanism of immunity – the presentation of antigens to the immune system. ASY-77A, enhances antigen presentation by targeting the soluble, extracellular form of Heat shock protein (HSP70) in the tumor microenvironment (TME).

In the TME, the function of dendritic cells (DCs) is suppressed through multiple mechanisms, thereby aiding and abetting tumor cell survival and precluding the development of robust anti-tumor immune responses. This contributes in many tumor types to either a blunting or complete abrogation of activity by immunotherapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). HSP70’s role is especially crucial in shuttling tumor-derived (or autoreactive or viral) antigens to DCs, which capture, process, and present tumor antigens to other immune cells in order to initiate the development of immune responses against all cancers (or self-antigens or viral antigens). ASY-77A initiates the shuttling of tumor neoantigens from HSP70 to DCs eliciting robust antigen presentation to circumvent tumor suppression mechanisms. 

Asylia's secondary program, ASY-87, represents potential for a universal ADC platform through its unique cell-surface HSP70 targeting. HSP70 is externalized on the surface of cancer cells due to proteotoxic stress, hypoxia, and acidosis in the TME; normal cells do not externalize HSP70. ASY-87 binds to its target across multiple tumor types, including lymphoma, breast, pancreatic and lung cancer.

We are pioneering a unique suite of antibodies against HSP70.

The chapter at NC State specializes in Custom Designs for recipients who would not benefit from a standard 3D printed device. As a university with a large number of engineering programs, many students in this chapter have engineering backgrounds, helping them take on unique and challenging cases to come up with a creative, novel solutions.

Regal Intel is a 501(c)(3) non-profit research consortium dedicated to bridging the gap between advanced technology and clinical practice. We ensure no patient remains undiagnosed due to statistical invisibility.

THE PROBLEM: The "Small N" Paradox
Standard AI systematically fails on the medical "Long Tail" because the patient count is too small for traditional models to learn . As a result, families residing in rural health networks face a devastating diagnostic odyssey. This invisibility affects three distinct clinical pillars:
1. Rare Diseases: Conditions suffering from extreme data sparsity.
2. Complex Diseases: Multi-morbidity clusters where common conditions intersect to create a statistically rare profile.
3. "Avid" Diseases: High-velocity pathologies that accelerate so rapidly they outpace standard clinical observation windows.

THE SOLUTION: Project JANUS
We deploy Sovereign Neuro-Symbolic AI to transform fragmented Real-World Data (RWD) into regulatory-grade clinical evidence (ALCOA+) . Unlike traditional "Black Box" AI, our methodology anchors algorithms in established medical rules and physical metabolic limits to prevent AI hallucinations . We utilize high-fidelity Synthetic Patient Twins to teach local models what rare and complex diseases look like, even if a specific clinic has never seen a case before.

ZERO-EXFILTRATION SOVEREIGNTY
We solve the data privacy deadlock. Through our hardware-attested federated learning infrastructure, Protected Health Information (PHI) never leaves the hospital firewall . We share only mathematical statistics, ensuring 100% data sovereignty.

OUR MISSION
We are cutting the diagnostic odyssey from 7 years to less than 48 hours for rural families. As a 100% non-profit organization, our exclusive focus is on clinical discovery and patient outcomes, not pharmaceutical sales or commercial patient panels.

Join the consortium and learn more at www.regalintel.com.

Description: Anvesana is developing first-in-class small molecules to treat patients suffering from genetic diseases caused by nonsense mutations. While each rare disorder affects a small number of individuals, collectively these conditions impact nearly 10% of the global population with a disproportionate impact on children. In 11% of patients with an orphan disease, the underlying genetic error is a nonsense mutation. This type of mutation introduces a premature termination codon (PTC) within the coding region of the mRNA. The presence of a PTC leads to the production of a truncated, non-functional protein, which is the root cause of disease. Anvesana is developing compounds that enable the translation machinery to read through these PTCs, restoring the production of full-length, functional proteins and offering a transformative therapeutic approach for patients with these otherwise intractable genetic diseases.

We have a green light from FDA to proceed with a Phase 2 dose-finding study. We hold issued and pending patents protecting this novel indication.

Patients are desperate for better treatment options. Over 4M women have been diagnosed with endometriosis, with two-thirds reporting significant functional impairment. There is no cure and current treatment options are bleak, skewing toward surgery and heavy use of opioids: three-quarters of patients undergo surgery (with nearly half opting for hysterectomy), one-third of patients take opioids, and one-in-ten patients take GnRH analogues, which chemically induce menopause. These options are expensive and none provide effective relief from the pain of endometriosis.

We've developed a reformulation of the well-known immunomodulator hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) that addresses endometriosis pathology at two points. It reduces pain by normalizing chronic inflammation and it inhibits lesion formation by reducing autophagy. Inflammation drives both pain sensitization and fibrosis, which causes adhesions. We’ve asked FDA to be indicated for relief of pain, as this is an established approval pathway which will allow us to get to market quickly.

Name: Throne Biotechnologies
Description:
Throne Biotechnologies (Throne) is a clinical-stage therapeutic company with a disruptive stem cell technology that can fundamentally reverse type 1 diabetes (T1D), alopecia areata (AA) and other autoimmune diseases through immune education of Stem Cell Educator therapy (“Educator Therapy”) at the root causes. Over last 10 years, international multicenter clinical trials in Spain, China, and the United States have strongly demonstrated the clinical safety and efficacy of Educator therapy in more than 200 patients aged from 3 to 70 years old. Currently, Throne has received three FDA-approved phase 2 INDs by using Educator therapy to treat T1D, AA, and severe COVID-19 patients. Specifically, our globally-patented technology is recognized as the leading “Practical Cure Project” for T1D out of 590 global projects (Juvenile Diabetes Cure Alliance (JDCA) 2021, New York). 

T1D is a T cell–mediated autoimmune disease that causes a deficit of islet beta cells. Millions of individuals worldwide have T1D, and incidence increases markedly since COVID-19 pandemic started. Recent clinical trials have highlighted the limits of conventional immune therapy and underscore the need for novel approaches that not only overcome multiple immune dysfunctions, but also help restore islet beta-cell function. To address these two key issues, Throne has developed a unique and novel Educator therapy by using a new type of cord blood-derived multipotent stem cells (CB-SC). With this patented technology, a patient’s blood is circulated through a blood cell separator, where the patient’s immune cells are co-cultured with adherent CB-SC in vitro, and returns “educated” immune cells to the patient’s circulation. Notably, Educator therapy is the only therapy to date to safely and efficiently correct autoimmunity and restore beta-cell function in T1D patients.

Description:

MGMR is a highly-efficient intracellular delivery vehicle, consisting of a stabile dispersion of hollow, nanoscale tubules approximately 1/10,000th the width of a human hair. The high aspect-ratio, nanoscale profile of MGMR allows it to readily penetrate cells without compromising membrane integrity or inducing cytotoxicity. Its high surface-to-volume ratio and tunable surface chemistry allow it to readily transport both small and large-molecular payloads into the cytoplasm, including growth factors, oligonucleotides, proteins and gene-editing complexes. 

Biopact has evaluated the cytotoxicity profile of MGMR across multiple cell-lines and investigated safety and efficacy in murine biodistribution and clearance models. Our in vivo studies demonstrate that MGMR is biologically-inert, well-tolerated and rapidly cleared from non-targeted tissues. In a murine therapeutic model, MGMR loaded with doxorubicin (Dox) demonstrated a remarkable capability to rapidly concentrate drug in targeted tissues and extend half-life of its molecular cargo.

Promising assessments of intracellular delivery performance in different eukaryotic cell-types suggest the potential for developing MGMR as a biomolecular delivery vehicle for various expression platforms and cell-factories of interest to agricultural and industrial applications, including mammalian cell-lines, yeasts, bacteria and plants. Robust cellular uptake observed with MGMR offers the potential to deliver molecular payloads to difficult-to-penetrate cell-types or those acutely sensitive to detergents and other conventional methods for transmembrane delivery.

Name: Raptamer Discovery Group, LLC
Description:
Raptamer Discovery Group, LLC is dedicated to the development and commercialization of aptamer technology and its products. Specifically, we develop synthetic affinity reagents called Raptamers for applications in life science research, diagnostics, and therapeutics. Raptamers provide the performance of monoclonal antibodies but avoid many of the problems associated with them.  

A Raptamer is an affinity agent (similar in function to an antibody) that is comprised of a single strand of DNA with non-DNA chemical modifications attached to one or more of the DNA bases. A Raptamer has much greater chemical diversity than a natural aptamer. Raptamers use combinations of chemically-modified DNA bases and backbones that typically cannot be amplified using PCR. This makes it impossible to generate Raptamers using the typical enzymatic processes used to select aptamers (e.g., SELEX). The diversity of the chemical functional groups in Raptamers provides much better interaction with a target, which typically results in better binding affinity and specificity.

Name: Cornerstone Genomics
Description:
Every amino acid substitution that survived 80 million years of primate evolution was tested by natural selection in organisms biochemically near-identical to us. If it persisted across 55 genera, biology already approved it. If it never appeared, biology hasn't permitted it.

CodeXome captures that record. Not as a model's prediction, but as a direct empirical observation, and delivers it as residue-level annotation that drops into existing genomic interpretation pipelines.

The result is a genuinely new evidence axis. Orthogonal to population frequency databases. Orthogonal to ML predictor scores. Orthogonal to deep vertebrate conservation tools. Adding CodeXome to a pipeline adds something none of those categories can provide: a biological fact about what nature actually tested and tolerated, at the specific amino acid position in question.

What this enables:
— 50–75% reduction in candidate variant lists before any manual review begins
— 10–40% of Variants of Uncertain Significance identified as likely benign by evolutionary evidence, across ~14,000 ClinVar genes
— Population-agnostic evidence that carries identical evidentiary weight regardless of patient ancestry

Validated at scale:
100% concordance with expert panel classifications across the ClinGen 52-gene study (2,689 SNVs) and ENIGMA/BRCA Exchange (10,699 BRCA1/2 variants).

Who we work with:
Research genomics labs, rare disease programs, biotech target validation teams, and bioinformatics cores integrating new annotation sources into existing pipelines.

CodeXome is a product of Cornerstone Genomics. Research use. Residue resolution. 19,244 genes. GRCh38.

KaRMa Exotechnologies is a women’s health biotech company built around a simple truth: preterm birth is devastating—for the baby, the mother, and the entire family. It disrupts lives, fractures expectations, and leaves long shadows on health and wellbeing. Yet for all of our medical advances, we still don’t have enough targeted, biology-informed options to prevent or treat these complications safely.
We’re working to change that by developing exosome-based therapeutics to address inflammatory drivers of preterm birth and related pregnancy complications. Our work centers on using extracellular vesicles—engineered exosomes—to deliver anti-inflammatory signals such as IL-10 directly to the tissues and interfaces that matter most in pregnancy, with the goal of improving outcomes while minimizing systemic toxicity.
Preterm birth is our first focus, but the need extends far beyond a single indication. Many female-specific inflammatory diseases across the reproductive lifespan have been underfunded and understudied. The same exosome-based platform we are building for preterm birth is designed to expand into other women’s health conditions where safer, more precise therapies are urgently needed.
At the same time, we know this field is bigger than any one company. KaRMa Exotechnologies also partners with others who want to harness the power of exosomes as drug delivery systems. Through research-use-only services in extracellular vesicles and reproductive immunology—including advanced in vitro and organ-on-chip models, custom assays, and exosome characterization—we help teams de-risk their own programs and move more confidently toward the clinic.
We are still early, but our direction is clear: better tools, better biology, and better options for women, mothers, and babies. What goes around, heals around.
