Description:
Combination drug therapies are central to modern medicine—but developing them remains inefficient, expensive, and uncertain.

Pharmaceutical teams must evaluate thousands of potential combinations with limited ability to reliably distinguish meaningful synergy from misleading signals. Traditional methods often produce conflicting results, making it difficult to prioritize the right combinations, select optimal dosing strategies, and confidently assess safety tradeoffs.

Duet Biosystems is changing how combination drug decisions are made.

Our platform is built on MuSyC (Multi-dimensional Synergy of Combinations), a patented framework that fundamentally improves how drug interactions are quantified. Unlike conventional approaches, MuSyC separates combination effects into distinct, mechanistically meaningful components—such as potency and efficacy—providing clearer, more actionable insight into how drugs work together.

We are extending this foundation with advanced machine learning and AI to help pharmaceutical teams:

Prioritize high-potential drug combinations earlier
Optimize dosing strategies with greater precision
Identify and evaluate safety tradeoffs before costly downstream studies
Reduce experimental burden and avoid low-value development paths

MuSyC has been cited in over 200 scientific publications and is under evaluation by the FDA as a Drug Development Tool, reflecting its potential to improve both internal decision-making and regulatory science.

Our mission is to become the global standard for combination drug development—enabling more confident decisions, more efficient R&D, and better outcomes for patients.

Description:
Maroon Biotech has developed a new category of pharmaceuticals called surfactant chaperones. This technology has the capability to restore structure and viability to cells disrupted by physical and chemical trauma. By reversing post-traumatic molecular alterations, Maroon Biotech’s technology promises to improve recovery from vehicular, military and other types of severe traumatic injuries, electrical shock and reperfusion injury. The technology has already demonstrated effectiveness at treating experimental spinal cord injury, myocardial infarction (heart attack) and brain injury.

Fundamentally, surfactant chaperones mimic behaviors exhibited by naturally occurring stress proteins that protect living systems after injury. The safety of certain synthetic surfactants that act as molecular chaperones has been proven over time. In particular, polymeric surfactant chaperones that are symmetric block copolymers of polyethylene oxide-polypropylene oxide-polyethylene oxide (PEO-PPO-PEO) have been used to reduce blood viscosity for more than fifty years. The capability of this surfactant to repair damaged cell membranes, however, was unknown until the late 1980’s when Raphael C. Lee, MD, ScD, DSc, Professor of Molecular Medicine and Surgery at the University of Chicago Pritzker School of Medicine, discovered its unique cell membrane healing properties.

Dr. Lee’s exciting discovery spurred research into clinical applications that continues today. The first product from Dr. Lee’s laboratory has achieved FDA approval for testing in electrical shock victims. Another product under development in partnership with Purdue University is expected to enable human victims of spinal cord injury to regain more of their sensory and motor functions. Because a protocol for treating spinal cord injury would likely qualify for orphan drug status, it could receive accelerated FDA approval and be on the market in four to five years.

Name: Rose Engine
Description:
Rose Engine is a computational discovery platform for RNA-era medicine.

Drug programs tend to fail late, and that failure often starts with a shaky first decision: which target to chase. The software teams rely on for that call is usually vague about its sources and quiet about its blind spots. The RNA-modification biology that many newer RNA therapies act on is barely touched by standard target-ID tools.
We built Rose Engine to take that first step seriously. It reads public evidence, including GEO expression data, ClinVar variants, ChEMBL pharmacology, and protein structures, then connects it into specific disease-mechanism gaps and therapeutic designs you can screen. Every result points back to a GEO accession and a PubMed ID. When the evidence runs out, the platform says "insufficient data" instead of filling the space with a guess.
Today it runs across 54 curated diseases. It has mapped 3,343 mechanistic gaps, narrowed those to 1,789 distinct research targets, and produced 134 drug-repurposing dossiers, 1,800 designs solutions that meet the gap requirements when existing public data makes it possible, and lastly builds restoration regimens. The system also has live query and design capabilities  that cover all allowed diseases and viruses outside the 54 curated offline. 

We work with discovery and translational biologists, computational teams, and RNA-therapeutic groups who want to see the reasoning behind a hypothesis, not just the hypothesis itself. 


Rose Engine is pre-clinical, in-silico decision-support software. It is not a clinical or diagnostic tool.

Description:
Definitive TNF Therapies is a preclinical-stage pharmaceutical company building the first orally bioavailable anti-TNF therapeutic.

TNF inhibitors treat over 7.5 million patients annually across rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, and other autoimmune conditions. The market exceeds $44 billion a year. Every approved product requires injection or infusion. Patients face needle burden, cold-chain logistics, immunogenicity-driven treatment failure, and serious infection risk. Oral alternatives (JAK inhibitors) carry FDA black box warnings for cardiovascular events, malignancy, and thrombosis.

No one has solved the oral anti-TNF problem because the biology sits in a molecular no-man's land: too large for traditional small molecules, too complex for simple reformulation of existing biologics. The only clinical-stage oral anti-TNF competitor has failed as monotherapy in both psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis, validating the hypothesis that partial TNF inhibition is insufficient.

Our approach is different. We use an enzymatic macrocyclic peptide platform, licensed from Sethera Therapeutics, to generate conformationally constrained molecules that combine biologic-grade target engagement with oral bioavailability. These are not reformulated biologics. They are purpose-built oral drugs designed from first principles.

Name: MindShield Tech
Description:
Hi! Our names are Lua Varner and Marina Caobianco. We are the co-founders of MindShield, a real time detection device for concussion risk. 

Addressing the challenge of real-time concussion risk detection in sports has the potential to transform athlete health, safety protocols, and the future of brain injury research, and confront a problem that has been often ignored or actively suppressed. For decades, major sports organizations such as the NFL have been criticized for downplaying or concealing research on concussions and chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), prioritizing profit and performance over health of the players. This suppression has left a gaping hole in our understanding and management of sports-related brain injuries, allowing preventable harm to persist across all levels of play. The problem remains an open wound in the world of athletics, marked by silence, delayed action, and a lack of accessible, real-time tools for detecting injury.

Our work aims to confront this issue head-on. By integrating AI-powered analytics with wearable technology, we provide real-time, objective assessments of head impact exposure, giving athletes, coaches, and medical staff immediate insights into concussion risk. This shift from reactive to proactive care helps prevent repeated injuries, supports safer return-to-play decisions, and generates high-quality data that would have the ability to support long-term research. Beyond individual health benefits, our platform has the power to influence safety standards, inform policy, and bring transparency to an issue that has been hidden for too long. By closing the gap in concussion detection, we are not just solving a technological problem, we are helping to repair the credibility and accountability of sports culture itself.

Name: OsteoPop
Description: Osteoporosis was long considered inevitable, merely a consequence of aging. Over the past 30 years, however, osteoclast modulating therapies have shown great promise in reducing fracture prevalence and improving patient quality of life. Unfortunately, more recent retrospective clinical studies have highlighted the prevalence of non-compliance amongst osteoporosis patients. It is estimated 60% of those initiating osteoporosis treatment become non-compliant shortly after beginning therapy. These individuals carry a nearly two-fold increased risk of fracture and associated alterations to medical expenses and quality of life. Despite clear clinical and pre-clinical evidence pointing to the efficacy and safety of osteoporosis drugs a variety of factors lead to patients still becoming non-compliant over long-term treatment intervals. Therefore, there is a clinical need to devise an integrated strategy to identify patients at risk for non-compliance, educate these patients in the risks associated with non-compliance, and track medication adherence over time. Using low power-consumption optical-sensing technologies, paired with electronic medical record integration, OsteoPop seeks to improve patient compliance and clinical outcomes for osteoporotic patients.

Name: ResearchOS
Description:
Your whole lab, in a notebook you actually own. ResearchOS is a free, open-source electronic lab notebook where every note, method, experiment, structure, sequence, and file is a plain file in a folder on your own computer. Nothing uploads unless you choose to sync, share, or co-edit, so private work stays on your machine and the app works fully offline.

One window stands in for a separate notebook, chemistry, cloning, stats, and ordering app. Draw a structure like you would in ChemDraw and pull the compound straight from PubChem. Open a plasmid in a SnapGene-style editor and let it design your cloning primers. Paste your data, run the test, and make a publication-ready figure. Every statistic is validated in public against scipy, R, and Prism, so you can trust the number you cite.

Most lab software bills hundreds of dollars per person per year, and your lab pays it again for every student who rotates through. Your data is the price, held on a cloud you cannot see. ResearchOS keeps your research in a folder you own, so leaving is just closing a folder, not a migration fight. It is also the honest answer to an NIH Data Management and Sharing Plan, because the data never has to leave your machine, and a one-click Zenodo deposit carries your ORCID and grant metadata when you are ready to share.

You can read exactly how it works. ResearchOS is open source under AGPLv3, and a public transparency page proves our math against Biopython, primer3, R, and Prism. The only thing that ever costs money is the optional cloud you choose to use, priced near what it costs us to run, so a whole lab is covered with no per-seat bill.

Built by two researchers tired of renting the notebook, shaped by work begun during a Distinguished Research Fellowship at UW-Madison, and run as a Wisconsin LLC and merchant of record, not a hobby link.

Own your research. Keep it in a folder you control, forever free.

Name: ADNIC Therapeutics
Description:
Mayo Clinic has created a next-generation antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) platform, validated by human clinical data. We are now seeking investors or strategic partners to accelerate the development of our platform for patient use. Dr. Svetomir Markovic, MD, PhD, leads the program.  

Current ADCs struggle to deliver effective drug doses to cancer cells while minimizing harm to normal tissues. This innovative platform, the modular Antibody-Drug Nano-Immuno Conjugate (ADNIC), overcomes this challenge by using albumin nanoparticles carrying a chemotherapeutic payload coated with a tumor-targeting monoclonal antibody.

Platform Summary 
•	Nanoparticle Core:  Albumin nanoparticles encapsulate the chemotherapeutic payload, creating a stable drug reservoir with enhanced loading capacity.
•	Antibody Coating: Tumor-targeting monoclonal antibodies coat the nanoparticle surface, enabling precise delivery to cancer cells.
•	Targeted Release: Upon binding to tumor cells, the conjugate delivers 100-fold more drug than traditional ADCs, maximizing therapeutic impact.

This modular architecture represents a fundamental innovation in ADC design, combining proven therapeutic components in a novel configuration that overcomes traditional limitations.

•	3 abstracts/posters

Description:
Cortexa Genomix Inc. is a Toronto-based precision diagnostics company developing advanced computational platforms to transform complex multi-omics data into clinically actionable disease risk insights.

Our platform integrates genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and clinical data to enable earlier, more accurate, and more interpretable disease risk prediction. Designed to operate at scale, the system supports diverse high-dimensional data sources—including RNA-seq, SNPs, sequence data, and public repositories such as GEO—and provides researchers and clinicians with robust computational tools to decode biological complexity and support effective prognostics.

Cortexa’s technology combines machine learning–driven feature engineering, pathway-level aggregation, graph-based biological modeling, and visualization to move beyond black-box analytics. By leveraging scalable architectures and graph technologies such as Neo4j and MongoDB, we bridge the gap between raw sequencing data and biologically interpretable, clinically relevant outcomes—supporting validation, reproducibility, and regulatory readiness.

Our initial application focus includes fertility, oncology, and neurological disorders, where early detection and mechanistic insight can significantly improve patient outcomes. Built and validated in Ontario through academic, clinical, and industry collaboration, Cortexa Genomix is advancing toward validated, AI-enabled diagnostic solutions that support a transition from reactive treatment to predictive, personalized healthcare.

The Musculoskeletal Outcomes Science Alliance for International Collaboration (MOSAIC) is a nonprofit startup and research accelerator building the first patient-centered, AI-ready musculoskeletal data network. We operate with the mission of a nonprofit and the speed of a startup, solving a critical bottleneck in orthopaedic innovation: health AI and digital twin models fail because the data powering them is fragmented, unstandardized, and missing the patient voice.

Our federated platform collects clinical, imaging, and patient-reported outcomes data across three tiers, from high-resolution research data at academic anchor sites to pragmatic clinical data from community practices to patient-contributed data at scale. As a research accelerator, MOSAIC gives investigators access to curated datasets, shared protocols, and collaborative infrastructure no single site could build alone.

Patients control their data and decide how it is used. MOSAIC delivers personalized insights back to them and empowers them to contribute to a collective effort that improves orthopaedic care for everyone.
MOSAIC is international from day one, with UConn Health as our founding partner and collaborators at leading academic institutions in the US and UK. We are committed to giving back to providers in low- and middle-income countries and rural US communities where access to outcomes data and decision support is most needed.

Our sustainability model is built on partnerships with ethical industry sponsors who share our commitment to putting patients first. Every dollar cycles back into the mission: better data, more sites, more patients empowered, everywhere.

Description:

The company's long-term vision is to develop systems that integrate more naturally with the human body, shifting from tools that are operated to technologies that function as intuitive extensions of the individual.

PonieTech operates through two subsidiaries. Acheulean Biotech is the company's biological platform, focused on tissue engineering, biomaterials, and bioprinting, the foundational science of building living, biocompatible systems. Looking Glass Robotics applies that platform to robotics, teleoperation, and human–machine interface development. 

Through Looking Glass Robotics, the company is developing Project Juvet (Patent Pending), a next-generation human–robot interface designed to address the embodiment gap in teleoperated systems, the challenge of enabling operators not only to control machines, but to receive meaningful, interpretable feedback from them.

Project Juvet explores a bioprinted, biocompatible interface approach to improving how signals are transmitted, interpreted, and returned between human and machine. The initial focus is on improving signal fidelity and interpretability at the human–machine interface under real-world conditions.

PonieTech is building toward a future where technology becomes a natural extension of the individual, grounded in biology rather than engineered around it.

PonieTech is currently pre-seed, with a $1M SAFE round open on AngelList (March 2026). A provisional patent has been filed on the core architecture. We are in ongoing dialogue with NIH NIBIB and exploring alignment with government research programs.

Investors and Angels, please visit us at www.ponietech.com for more information.

Name: Lucks Lab
Description:
The Lucks Lab develops high-throughput methods to measure RNA folding and function and uses this data to develop new AI RNA design models. Using these models, we design and develop RNA-based technologies including biosensors, programmable genetic tools, therapeutics, and point-of-use diagnostics. We partner with communities to field test and co-develop our technologies to achieve real-world impact.

Our research seeks to reveal the principles that enable biological systems to sense and adapt to changing environments and to understand how we can use these principles to engineer synthetic biological systems that benefit humankind. A focal point of our work is RNA –a fundamental component of all living systems that enacts genetic, regulatory and catalytic functions by folding into intricate shapes within cells. An overarching approach of our work is to link fundamental discovery to synthesis: to distill the complexity of natural biological systems into design principles that can then be used to build sophistication within synthetic systems. This dual discovery/synthesis approach allows us to interrogate molecular systems in powerful ways, with each approach informing the other in a cycle of increasing understanding.

Research Areas
- Understanding and Engineering Dynamic RNA Regulatory Elements
- Quantitative Modeling and High-throughput RNA Structural Biology
- Impacting Human Health with Synthetic Biotechnologies
- Design of Dynamic Functional RNAs through Machine Learning

Name: Definitive TNF Therapies
Description:
Definitive TNF Therapies is a preclinical pharmaceutical company working on the first orally bioavailable anti-TNF therapy. The goal is right there in the name: build the definitive anti-TNF treatment.

TNF inhibitors changed how autoimmune diseases are treated. More than 7.5 million patients receive them every year for rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, and other conditions. The market is worth more than $44 billion annually.

But every approved anti-TNF therapy still has to be injected or infused. That means needles and cold-chain logistics, along with immunogenicity-related loss of response and serious infection risk. JAK inhibitors provide an oral alternative, but carry FDA boxed warnings for cardiovascular events, malignancy, and thrombosis.

The reason oral TNF inhibition remains unsolved is molecular. TNF falls between traditional small molecules and biologics: it is beyond the reach of the former, while the latter cannot simply be reformulated as pills. The only clinical-stage oral anti-TNF competitor has failed as monotherapy in both psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis. That supports the conclusion that partial TNF inhibition is not enough.

Our approach starts with a different kind of molecule. We use an enzymatic macrocyclic peptide platform licensed from Sethera Therapeutics to make conformationally constrained molecules designed to combine biologic-grade target engagement with oral bioavailability. These are not biologics put into pill form. They are oral drugs built specifically for TNF.

Definitive TNF Therapies is based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

Name: IsletRegen, LLC
Description:
IsletRegen is a Charlottesville-based, preclinical biotechnology company developing regenerative and immune-directed therapies for type 1 diabetes. Our lead program, RegenPepTM, is a synthetic peptide therapeutic designed to address two central drivers of the disease in a single treatment: autoimmune damage to insulin-producing beta cells and the loss of beta-cell function.

Our approach is designed to combine immune protection with beta-cell regeneration, with the goal of preserving and restoring the body’s natural ability to produce insulin. RegenPep is supported by proof-of-principle findings across human pancreatic tissue, human islet, and preclinical mouse models.

IsletRegen is currently advancing candidate selection, optimization, and the translational work required to support future IND-enabling development and clinical evaluation in early-stage type 1 diabetes.

Name: Futile Flower
Description:
About Futile Flower

Futile Flower is committed to advancing plant genetics and precision cultivation through cutting-edge research and development. Located in southwest Missouri, we specialize in strain hunting and phenotype development, offering licensed companies tailored research solutions to discover and cultivate exceptional varieties for their operations.

Our mission is to be the trusted partner for operators seeking unique, high-performing cultivars. By delivering detailed, data-driven insights, we enable our clients to make informed decisions when integrating new genetics into their production. With a strong emphasis on compliance, integrity, and innovation, we ensure that every aspect of development meets industry standards and client expectations.

What We Do:
Strain Hunting & Phenotype Development:
Our core service involves cultivating and analyzing client-provided seeds to identify cultivars that align with specific growth and market criteria. Using detailed phenotypic evaluations and measurable data, we provide clients with a clear understanding of each variety’s potential for success. We maintain rigorous quality control, ensuring only the best cultivars move forward.

Tissue Culture & Genetic Preservation:
We safeguard our clients' genetic assets through advanced tissue culture techniques. After identifying successful strains, we offer vegetative clones and preserve the genetic material for future production. This ensures the long-term availability and quality of these unique cultivars.

Compliance & Integrity:
Futile Flower operates with full compliance to all regulatory requirements, responsibly managing byproducts from our research processes. Our NDA agreements protect the exclusive genetic rights of our clients, ensuring complete confidentiality and security.

At Futile Flower, we are passionate about shaping the future of cultivation with research-driven solutions, genetic innovation, and an unwavering commitment to quality and integrity.

Name: TDSR-MetaBolics
Description:
Metabolics is a research branch of TDSR LLC focused on biological science in the areas of metabolic function and how it relates to health and disease. We endeavor to study from the macro scale of foods we eat and how it is processed, to cellular scale at the mitochondrial level and the effects of mitochondrial disfunction in disease. 

We believe this is a critical area of research that is core to improving overall human health and quality of life. 

Most disease research focuses on symptoms and after the fact fighting of various ailments. We believe it is better to understand root cause and target prevention. We do this through research conducted at Metabolics, along with deep studies of existing journals and the ongoing research of others to try to piece together larger pictures that can be easily missed when focusing on the details.
